incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT — elevated request latency observed for /v1/generate (hosted). Auto-detection triggered at 1942103333. Severity: S2. Paging oncall team: @Maya Chen, @Sarah Nguyen

Maya Chen: got the page, looking now. Any known deploys?

Alex Park: no deploys in the last 30m. Seeing queue length jump on batcher-01 and batcher-03. p95 token latency spiked from ~120ms -> ~650ms for several tenants.

Sarah Nguyen: pulling metrics. KV cache miss rate rising ~3x, batch window growth seen — average batch size up 2.2x. Could be a traffic pattern change increasing prefix variance.

Maya Chen: ok. Quick risk triage: do we want to change batching parameters live (reduce window to cut latency) or put a temporary route-level rate-limit to protect SLOs? Both?

Jon Patel: recommend immediate batching tweak + short rate cap for noisy tenants. Batching tweak less invasive and fast to roll.

Alex Park: agree. I'm prepping a canary change to batch_config for a single region. Current: `batch_window_ms: 40`, `max_batch_tokens: 2048`. Plan: set `batch_window_ms: 12` and `max_batch_tokens: 1024` for canary group.

Maya Chen: can you run the canary against us-east-1 batcher-03? I'll watch latency and error rate.

Alex Park: deploying now. Command: 
```
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/batcher-03 BATCH_WINDOW_MS=12 MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=1024 --record
```

incident-bot: Deploy started for batcher-03 canary at 1942103348.

Sarah Nguyen: logs show queue length dropping immediately on canary. p50 token latency stable, p95 falling from 640ms -> 210ms for canary traffic. No increase in 5xx so far.

Luis Ortega: support note — several enterprise customers reported interactive timeouts. I'm ready to notify them if we put a tenant-level cap.

Maya Chen: good. Alex, after we observe canary for 2m and confirm signal, roll change to all batchers in us-east-1. Also create ephemeral route quota: `rate_limit_per_minute: 1200` for top noisy app IDs as backup.

Alex Park: canary looks stable at +90s. Rolling to east region: 
```
for ns in batcher-01 batcher-02 batcher-03; do kubectl -n inference set env deploy/$ns BATCH_WINDOW_MS=12 MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=1024; done
```

incident-bot: Rollout started at 1942103362. Monitoring metrics.

Sarah Nguyen: after rollout, p95 global fell to ~230ms, overall throughput down ~28% (fewer tokens processed/sec). Error rate unchanged. KV miss rate still elevated but less amplification.

Maya Chen: that's in line with expectations — we traded throughput for tail latency. Need to notify customers in impacted class: interactive, low-latency apps. Luis, can you draft a short message to the top 10 tenants that may see throughput drop but better responsiveness? Keep it technical and include rollback plan.

Luis Ortega: draft ready, posting to #support-escalations for review.

Jon Patel: follow-up mitigation idea — enable short-term per-tenant burst tokens so bursty clients can finish requests while global batching smaller. Also schedule a follow-up to tune quantization/kv caching to restore throughput later.

Maya Chen: agreed. Also setting an automation to revert batching change if error rate > 1% or p95 > 600ms for 2 consecutive minutes.

Alex Park: creating quick rollback policy: 
```
POST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/rollouts
{
  "target": "batching-config",
  "canary": false,
  "values": {"BATCH_WINDOW_MS": 40, "MAX_BATCH_TOKENS": 2048}
}
```

incident-bot: Automation hook configured. Revert criteria: error_rate > 1% OR p95 > 600ms for 120s.

Sarah Nguyen: monitoring notes: successful mitigation validated at 1942103368. Latency now within SLO for interactive customers. Throughput impact noted and will be communicated.

Maya Chen: oncall handoff — @Maya Chen to @Sarah Nguyen in 10m. I'll leave a runbook entry under incidents/1942103333 for postmortem. Items: root cause hypothesis (traffic shape + KV cache miss storm + batching policy too permissive), short-term fix (reduce batch window, tenant rate caps), medium-term actions (cache warming, adaptive batch sizing, tenant-level QoS), customers notified.

Sarah Nguyen: taking point for next 2 hours. Will keep monitoring and collect traces. Please add any sample trace ids below if you see anomalies.

Alex Park: sample trace id for a slow request pre-mitigation: `trace-0a7f3c`. Will attach logs to the runbook.

Luis Ortega: sent notification to affected tenants at 1942103370 — included expected impact and ETA for follow-up optimization.

Maya Chen: thanks team. Marking this thread as incident-handled for paging; SRs staying open for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
